::: {#rem-expectation-generalizes-population-mean}
#### The expectation extends the population mean to populations without a finite size

Group the units of a [finite](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-finite-set) population by their values,
as in the proof of @prp-population-mean-expectation:
$n_y$ of the $n$ units have value $y$.
Then the [population mean](#def-expectation) is

$$
\avgin a_i = \sum_{y} y \cd \frac{n_y}{n},
$$

a [sum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-summation) over the distinct values, each weighted by its relative frequency $n_y / n$.
For a unit [chosen at random](probability-basics.qmd#def-random-choice),
that relative frequency is the [probability mass function](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) of its value:
$\P(Y = y) = n_y / n$.

The [definition of expectation](#def-expectation) keeps the [formula](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/expressions-algorithms.html#def-closed-form-expression)
and replaces the relative frequencies with [probabilities](probability-basics.qmd#def-probability):
$\E{X} = \sum_{x} x \cd \P(X = x)$.
That version no longer needs a population size $n$ to divide by,
so it also covers [random variables](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable) that no finite population produces:

- a [discrete random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-discrete-rv) with infinitely many possible values,
  such as the number of trials before the first success,
  where the sum has infinitely many terms;
- a [continuous random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-continuous-rv),
  where every single value has probability $0$,
  so the [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) takes the place of the relative frequencies
  and an [integral](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#def-riemann-integral) takes the place of the sum:
  $\E{X} = \int x \cd \p(X = x)\,dx$.

So the [expectation](#def-expectation) is the population mean of a population that may be infinite,
described by its [distribution](random-variables.qmd#def-cdf) rather than by a list of its units.

:::
